close_reason: Deferred. parse_rnews_batch_plain alone returning Vec<&[u8]> saves nothing — parse_rnews_batch still calls .to_vec() to produce Vec<Vec<u8>>. Eliminating copies requires changing the public signature, a breaking API change. Added explanatory comment at rnews.rs allocation site. Revisit when the public API is versioned.
description:
parse_rnews_batch_plain (rnews.rs line 181) calls `input[pos..article_end].to_vec()` for every article, copying each article's bytes into a new heap allocation. The caller (rnews_main.rs) already holds the full batch in `stdin_bytes` (up to 1 GiB). The parsed Vec<Vec<u8>> is a second copy of that data, so peak RSS can reach 2× the batch size.

For the common case (a few MB batch) this is harmless. For a max-size batch (1000 articles × 1 MiB = 1 GiB) peak memory is 2 GiB.

Fix: change parse_rnews_batch_plain to return `Vec<Range<usize>>` (byte ranges into the original input) or `Vec<&[u8]>` (slices with lifetime tied to the input), eliminating the copy. The caller can iterate over slices without owning each article. This requires a lifetime on the return type but is straightforward.
title: parse_rnews_batch: article bytes are copied into Vec<Vec<u8>>, doubling peak memory
